name: teamwork-tasks-from-session
description: Turn the work you just did in a Claude Code session into a Teamwork.com Projects task (plus optional subtasks) — for the common case where you start solving a problem in Claude Code before a task even exists. The skill reconstructs what the session accomplished (git commits + working-tree diff made since the session started, changed files, repo shape, and the live conversation context), drafts a main task in the canonical WAME format ([preamble] → HR → ## Akceptačné kritériá → HR → ## Cieľ → HR → ## Technický popis — the same Plan-Mode technical write-up produced by teamwork-task-analyze), proposes 2–6 atomic subtasks when the estimate exceeds 240 min and the work has natural cut points, and computes a `wame-estimate-v2` estimate (one number against fixed anchors, 15-minute step, 480-minute cap) shown next to the real logged session time — this plugin is the methodology's only measured feedback loop. The acceptance criteria carry the applicable cross-cutting requirements shared with teamwork-task-test (reachability via a menu entry and links from related screens, security, performance, UI/UX) — stated as delivered only when the diff proves it, otherwise listed as open and never claimed; the technical plan records the installed framework versions and the idioms the diff actually used (plan only, never an acceptance criterion). It logs the REAL session duration back to Teamwork: the session start is detected from a bundled SessionStart hook that records each session's wall-clock start into the shared config dir, falling back (in order) to the end of today's last timelog, to the newest session transcript's first timestamp, and finally to asking the user — always shown as a proposal that can be edited before anything is written; the logged block is clamped so it never overlaps existing timelogs. If no Teamwork URL is passed the skill asks where to file the work; a project or tasklist URL creates a new main task there, a single-task URL files the session work as a subtask of that task. Everything is shown in a full preview + confirmation gate before any write, and after creating the task the skill asks per run what to do with the board state (leave it / move it to the done column — the shared board_workflow target, Done - Local by default with fallbacks Internal testing → Testing, the same column teamwork-task moves cards to / mark complete). Reuses the shared API token config at ~/.claude/plugins/data/teamwork-task-wamesk/config.json with the rest of the Teamwork plugin family (teamwork-task, teamwork-task-test, teamwork-task-analyze, teamwork-tasks-from-desk, teamwork-tasks-from-dnr) — set the token once. Time logs are sequential, non-overlapping and 5-minute-aligned, written in a business tone with an optional (commit: <hash>) suffix. Never pushes git, never sends anything to a customer, never silently overwrites an estimate, and never logs time without an explicit confirmation.
